review.title: An agent instruction file has provenance, or it is not an instruction
review.acceptance: Repository validation detects any AGENTS.md or CLAUDE.md under a working directory that is not on an explicit, reviewed allowlist, and the authoritative instruction hierarchy is stated somewhere an agent reads before it starts. THE CONCRETE CASE: apps/web/AGENTS.md is GENERATED BY next dev and instructs agents to read node_modules/next/dist/docs/ before writing code. Nothing acted on it, and it is almost certainly benign. The finding is not that file -- it is that framework tooling can write an instruction file into a directory agents treat as authoritative, which makes a dependency's postinstall a path into the control plane's instruction surface. Required: the allowlist names each legitimate instruction file and who owns it, so an unowned one is a validation failure rather than a judgement call; generated instruction files are either gitignored and removed or allowlisted after being read, and the choice is recorded per file; validation fails on an unexpected file rather than warning, because a warning in a passing run is not a control; a regression plants an unexpected AGENTS.md and observes the failure, since a detector nobody has seen fire is not known to work; and the instruction hierarchy is written down -- which file wins, and that nothing under node_modules is ever authoritative. WHAT THIS TASK MUST NOT DO: silently delete a file a framework needs, or treat allowlisting as review. An allowlisted generated file must have been READ by a human or an agent that reports what it says.

recommended.title: Contract module boundaries
recommended.acceptance: Shared vocabularies live in their own leaf modules, domain contracts live in one module each, index.ts is a re-export-only compatibility barrel rather than the authoritative public surface, and a wildcard exports map lets a new domain contract be added without touching package metadata or the barrel; no cycle-driven z.lazy remains and structural regressions prove the boundary rather than merely reflecting it; no schema behaviour changes

recommended.title: Profile model

recommended.title: Provider outbound HTTP resolves, classifies and pins its destination
recommended.acceptance: THE CANONICAL HOST AND NETWORK POLICY MOVES TO A DEPENDENCY-LEAF PACKAGE, @liberty/net-policy, and both existing classifiers consume it. This replaces the original design, which was 'provider-sdk adopts media-inspection's resolve-and-pin control'; that is preserved in acceptanceOriginal and is NOT to be implemented. WHY THE DESIGN CHANGED, because the reason is the whole point: PL-0709 had to import provider-sdk's classifyHost from media-inspection BY DEEP RELATIVE PATH to write its agreement test, since classifyHost is not exported from packages/provider-sdk/src/index.ts and that package's exports field is a bare ./src/index.ts with no subpaths. The reviewer accepted that import FOR THAT TEST ONLY AT THAT TREE and ruled it is not an acceptable permanent boundary. Making media-inspection depend on provider-sdk, or provider-sdk on media-inspection while media-inspection imports provider-sdk to compare, CREATES OR INVITES A WORKSPACE DEPENDENCY CYCLE -- PL-0710 has provider-sdk adopting media-inspection's authoriseFetchTarget, so the arrow already points the other way. A lower shared layer with NO dependency on provider-sdk or media-inspection is the shape that works. REQUIRED, extraction half: the canonical host and IP classification vocabulary and its normalisation move into @liberty/net-policy; provider-sdk consumes that shared classifier; media-inspection consumes that shared classifier; PL-0709's deep cross-package test import is REMOVED; and the agreement test becomes unnecessary as two implementations become one -- replace it with tests of the shared classifier PLUS package-boundary tests proving both consumers actually import it, because an extraction nothing imports is a third copy rather than a merge. The package name may follow repository convention, but the package must be a dependency leaf. REQUIRED, resolve-and-pin half, unchanged from the original and each clause a separate way host-literal checking fails: DNS resolution before the outbound connection; EVERY resolved address classified, not just the first; refusal if ANY resolved address is private, loopback, link-local or reserved, unless an explicitly permitted local-only path applies; the connection PINNED to the approved resolved address so DNS rebinding cannot change the destination between check and connect; resolution, classification and pinning repeated PER REDIRECT HOP; and TLS CERTIFICATE HOSTNAME VERIFICATION AND SNI REMAIN AGAINST THE ORIGINAL HOSTNAME, NOT THE PINNED IP -- pinning the transport must not turn into verifying the wrong name. Regressions required for public-name-to-private-IP, DNS rebinding, mixed public and private answer sets, and translated-address cases. ALSO IN SCOPE BECAUSE THE EXTRACTION PUTS IT IN PLAY: pin.ts's normaliseHost does not fold the DNS root label. It is safe today because both sides of that comparison come from the same URL object so they carry or omit the dot together, and a mismatch refuses the connection -- but it is a third canonicaliser, and this is the task that removes the others. WHY THIS IS P0: F1, F7 and F8 were three host spellings in one function, and F12 was a fourth spelling in a SECOND function written specifically to avoid duplicating the first. The duplication got in anyway -- not as a copied classifier but as a copied assumption about what a hostname string is. A check comparing a string against literals is only ever as complete as the list of spellings whoever wrote it thought of; resolve-and-pin classifies the address a resolver returned, which has one spelling. FOLDED IN 2026-09-20 from the PL-0305 handoff's remaining off-surface item, because this task already owns both packages and the packaging metadata: @liberty/media-inspection's exports field has no ./http subpath, so importing @liberty/catalog-ingestion from apps/web pulls hls.ts into the program and needs an ambient m3u8-parser shim reached by a triple-slash reference in the ingestion package's index. That reference is the smallest honest fix from inside that package and is not the fix. THE SAME DEFECT SHAPE AS THE ONE THIS TASK EXISTS FOR: provider-sdk's classifyHost is unreachable from outside its package for exactly the same reason, a bare ./src/index.ts exports field with no subpaths, which is why PL-0709 had to import it by deep relative path. Give @liberty/media-inspection the subpath exports its consumers actually need and remove the triple-slash workaround, and make sure @liberty/net-policy is published with the subpaths ITS two consumers need rather than repeating the omission in the new package.

recommended.acceptanceOriginal: Provider outbound HTTP adopts the existing @liberty/media-inspection resolve-and-pin control (authoriseFetchTarget / nodePinnedFetch) instead of classifying host literals. Required, and each clause is a separate way host-literal checking fails: DNS resolution happens BEFORE the outbound connection; EVERY resolved address is classified, not just the first; the request is refused if ANY resolved address is private, loopback, link-local or reserved, unless an explicitly permitted local-only path applies; the connection is PINNED to the approved resolved address, so DNS rebinding cannot change the destination between the check and the connect; redirects repeat resolution, classification and pinning PER HOP; and TLS hostname verification and SNI are not regressed -- pinning to an address must still present and verify the name. Tests are required for public-name-to-private-IP, DNS rebinding, mixed public/private answer sets, and translation-prefix cases. WHY THIS IS P0 AND WHY IT IS FILED NOW: F1, F7 and F8 are three defects of ONE SHAPE in one function -- a host spelling the string comparisons did not anticipate, each reading as public, none findable by reading. A check that compares a string against literals is only ever as complete as the list of spellings whoever wrote it thought of. Resolve-and-pin classifies the address a resolver returned, which has one spelling.
recommended.architectureAmendedBeforeClaim: AMENDED 2026-09-19 BY gpt-architect's explicit round-50 direction, BEFORE THE CLAIM, and the reviewer was equally explicit that it must be done before rather than after: 'Amend PL-0710's allowedPaths BEFORE CLAIM to include the new shared package and the minimum workspace/package metadata needed to create it. Do not widen it after implementation has already started.' The surface accordingly grew from ['packages/provider-sdk/**','docs/SECURITY.md'] to include packages/net-policy/** (the new leaf package), packages/media-inspection/** (the second consumer, and the home of the deep import being removed), and the minimum workspace metadata: package.json and package-lock.json because npm workspaces is 'apps/*, packages/*' and a new package needs the lockfile regenerated, tsconfig.base.json for path mapping, turbo.json for the pipeline, and docs/ARCHITECTURE.md because a new package in the dependency graph is an architecture fact. THIS IS A WIDE SURFACE AND IT IS RESERVED BEFORE THE WORK STARTS ON PURPOSE -- an extraction that discovers its consumers mid-flight is exactly the case the no-widening-after-start rule exists for.
recommended.surfaceCorrectedBeforeClaim: CORRECTED 2026-09-20, BEFORE THE CLAIM: root package.json REMOVED from allowedPaths. I declared it in the round-50 amendment as 'the minimum workspace metadata needed to create the package', and that was a guess rather than a finding. THE EVIDENCE SAYS IT IS NOT NEEDED: root package.json declares workspaces as the pure globs ['apps/*','packages/*'], so packages/net-policy is picked up with no edit; it has no script naming any package path and no @liberty dependency; and tsconfig.base.json carries NO compilerOptions.paths at all, so there is no path map to extend either -- packages resolve through the workspace links. package-lock.json, which genuinely must be regenerated, stays. Removing a needed path to dodge a reservation is the move this project does not make; removing an unneeded one I declared speculatively is correcting my own over-declaration, and the right time to do it is before the claim rather than after. FLAGGED TO THE REVIEWER RATHER THAN TREATED AS SETTLED -- if gpt-architect reads this as manufacturing readiness, the entry goes back and PL-0710 waits for PL-AI-0008. recommended.title: Provider health contract
recommended.acceptance: A provider with zero observations reports unknown with a null observed success rate and a zero sample count, never a mid-range score and never a pass; any prior used to rank an unobserved provider is labelled as a prior rather than presented as measured availability; degraded-but-usable is a state distinct from up and down; health output is pure over the observations plus an explicit policy version, with no hidden wall-clock decay; and health never affects entitlement, so a provider at perfect health still cannot make an unauthorized candidate eligible

typecheck.evidence: turbo run typecheck --filter @liberty/provider-sdk exit 0 under pinned Node 22 resolved via npx node@22.

unit.evidence: turbo run test --filter @liberty/provider-sdk exit 0 under pinned Node 22: zero observations yielding unknown with a null observed rate and a zero sample count, a prior labelled rather than presented as measurement at the same ranking number as a measured value, the degraded band held distinct from up and down, purity over observations plus an explicit policy version with Date.now replaced by a thrower to prove no wall clock is read, whole-report permutation invariance under generated policies, monotonicity in each count, and a compile-time guard that no health type can carry entitlement.

recommended.title: Production composition registers the catalog ingestion runtime
recommended.acceptance: A hosted deployment that is configured for a real catalog source actually gets one: something in the production composition root calls registerCatalogIngestionRuntime with a runtime built next to the Node pinned-fetch construction. PL-0305 made the application CAPABLE of hosting the real source and the reviewer accepted that as complete; what remains is that NOTHING CALLS THE REGISTRATION, so a hosted deployment still answers no_metadata_source_configured -- a true statement about the deployment rather than about the registry, and the exact gap this task owns. Required: the runtime is built from the existing pinned-fetch transport rather than a second fetch path; NO CREDENTIAL OR API KEY IS INTRODUCED, since the initial source needs none and an ambient key would be the hidden credentialed source PL-0305's review forbade; an unconfigured deployment must STILL refuse by name rather than silently acquiring a default; and a regression must drive the composition root and observe a configured resolution, because a registration nobody has watched fire is not known to work. OUT OF SCOPE: persistent scheduling and storage, which is PL-0309, and the rights register, which is not a coding task. NOTE BEFORE CLAIMING: the exact composition-root file may not exist yet; the declared surface names the likely homes and must be corrected before the claim rather than widened after, on the PL-0710 precedent.

recommended.title: Playback-session candidate wire bounds match StreamCandidate bounds
recommended.acceptance: playbackSessionCandidateSchema uses THE SAME AUTHORITATIVE id and providerId limits as the StreamCandidate contract -- the exported MAX_STREAM_CANDIDATE_ID_CHARS and MAX_STREAM_CANDIDATE_PROVIDER_ID_CHARS -- and NOT copied numeric literals. PL-0708 exported those constants for exactly this reason; a copied literal would recreate the defect one layer out, which is the defect this task exists to close. Required: an oversized resolved candidate CANNOT RE-EXPAND ON THE SESSION WIRE after passing through another producer seam, which is the actual risk -- the contract bound governs what a provider may produce, and a second unbounded restatement downstream means the bound stops at the seam; fixture and Wikidata legitimate identifiers remain accepted, because a bound that rejects a real upstream id is an outage rather than a fix; tests cover the EXACT MAXIMUM, MAXIMUM PLUS ONE, and the serialized response, since a bound tested only from above does not prove the boundary is where it is claimed to be; reason and error output does not echo the oversized value; and NO SECOND INDEPENDENT BOUND VOCABULARY IS INTRODUCED. Note while working: playbackSessionCandidateSchema also carries unbounded uri and mimeType. They are not named in the reviewer's acceptance and are not in scope by default -- if they warrant bounds, say so and let the reviewer rule rather than adding them quietly.
